correctness.rationale: Direct eight-state generator eigenfunction reconstruction yields the quoted stationary two-sided PSD. The exact rational identity \(G(z)-G(0)=z(C+Bz-Az^2)/(\text{positive denominator})\) is checked symbolically over rational instances and derived by common denominators. A strictly increasing polynomial witness on the only possible positive-frequency window establishes all-u threshold uniqueness; the bias threshold is a unique zero of an explicitly strictly increasing function. A positive-vertex double-root condition classifies finite-frequency onset; exact quartic factorization checks the endpoint. Small-parameter expansions and strict separation at threshold prove the global peak square-root and quarter-root laws. The included standalone program replays 783 finite tests, supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: In the original eight-state biochemical example the low-frequency spectral curvature was used as a convenient sufficient detector for positive oscillation efficiency, but does not decide global performance. The new exact threshold resolves the missing region where a zero-frequency local maximum coexists with a stronger finite-frequency global peak. Its unique bias boundary separates continuous, quarter-root tricritical, and finite-jump frequency selection, including finite reverse hopping rates. These exact structural distinctions make the result more than a renamed inequality or a mere numeric optimization.
